messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Malayalam, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Output: ONE Markdown table only (no prose). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] In [Target Requirement]: make comparative ordering+degree explicit and add a 1-line literal back-translation check.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement (Malayalam morphosyntax) | |-------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------| | **Tant'** | Intensifier of “amara” (so) | Use adverb **ഇത്ര** *ithra* before the adjective; *ഇത്ര* + *കയ്പ്പുള്ള* → “so bitter”. **Back‑translation:** “so”. | | **è** (1st) | Copular link (present) | Insert present‑tense copula **ആണ്** *āṇ* after the subject (null pronoun). **Back‑translation:** “is”. | | **amara** | Predicate adjective “bitter” | Render as **കയ്പ്പുള്ള** *kayppuḷḷa* (bitter) agreeing in gender‑neutral form; placed after copula. **Back‑translation:** “bitter”. | | **che** | Comparative subordinator (“that”) | Use comparative particle **കാൾ** *kāl* to introduce clause; functions as “that”. **Back‑translation:** “that”. | | **poco** | Degree adverb “little” (slight) | Translate with **കുറച്ച്** *kuṟacc* placed before comparative marker. **Back‑translation:** “little”. | | **è** (2nd) | Copular link in comparative clause (present) | Same as above: **ആണ്** *āṇ* after subject “death”. **Back‑translation:** “is”. | | **più** | Comparative adverb “more” | Use **കൂടുതൽ** *kūṭuthal* after degree adverb; marks “more”. **Back‑translation:** “more”. | | **morte** | Noun “death”, comparative subject (greater) | Translate as **മരണം** *maraṇaṁ* (neuter noun) in nominative; serves as subject of comparative clause. **Back‑translation:** “death”. | | **ma** | Coordinating conjunction “but” | Render with **പക്ഷേ** *pakṣē* linking clauses. **Back‑translation:** “but”. | | **per** | Preposition of purpose “in order to” | Use purpose marker **വേണ്ടി** *veṇṭi* attached to infinitive verb. **Back‑translation:** “for”. | | **trattar** | Infinitive “to treat/discuss” | Use verbal noun **ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ** *carcha ceyyān* (to discuss) in infinitive form; takes **വേണ്ടി**. **Back‑translation:** “to treat”. | | **del** | Partitive “of the” (ben) | Combine preposition **യുടെ** *yude* with definite article omitted; attaches to noun. **Back‑translation:** “of the”. | | **ben** | Noun “good” (object of discussion) | Translate as **നല്ലത്** *nallat* (the good) in accusative/oblique case **നല്ലത്‌ക്ക്** *nallatkk* when governed by **ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ**. **Back‑translation:** “good”. | | **ch'** | Relative pronoun “that” | Use relative marker **എന്ന** *enna* after noun. **Back‑translation:** “that”. | | **i'** | Pronoun “I” (subject) | Render as **ഞാൻ** *ñān* (1st‑person pronoun). **Back‑translation:** “I”. | | **vi** | Locative adverb “there” | Translate as **അവിടെ** *aviṭe* (locative). **Back‑translation:** “there”. | | **trovai** | Past tense “found” (passato remoto) | Use simple past **കണ്ടു** *kaṇṭu* (found) with 1st‑person suffix **കണ്ടു** (no extra suffix). **Back‑translation:** “found”. | | **dirò** | Future tense “I will tell” | Use future auxiliary **പറയും** *paṟayam* (will say/tell) with 1st‑person suffix. **Back‑translation:** “I will tell”. | | **de** | Partitive “of the” (l'altre) | Same as **del** → **യുടെ** *yude* attached to noun. **Back‑translation:** “of the”. | | **l'altre** | Determiner + adjective “the other” | Translate as **മറ്റുള്ള** *maṟṟuḷḷa* (other) with definite sense implied; no article in Malayalam. **Back‑translation:** “the other”. | | **cose** | Noun “things” (plural) | Render as **വസ്തുക്കൾ** *vasthukkaḷ* (things) in accusative/oblique case **വസ്തുക്കൾക്ക്** *vasthukkaḷkk* when governed by **പറയും**. **Back‑translation:** “things”. | | **ch'** (2nd) | Relative pronoun “that” | Same as above: **എന്ന** *enna*. **Back‑translation:** “that”. | | **i'** (2nd) | Pronoun “I” (subject) | **ഞാൻ** *ñān*. **Back‑translation:** “I”. | | **v'** | Locative adverb “there” (again) | **അവിടെ** *aviṭe*. **Back‑translation:** “there”. | | **ho** | Auxiliary “have” (present) for perfect | Use auxiliary **ഉണ്ട്** *uṇṭ* in perfect construction; combined with past participle. **Back‑translation:** “have”. | | **scorte** | Past participle “seen” (scorte) | Use past participle **കണ്ട** *kaṇṭa* (seen) agreeing with object; combined with **ഉണ്ട്** → **കണ്ടിട്ടുണ്ട്** *kaṇṭiṇṭuṇṭ* (have seen). **Back‑translation:** “seen”. |
**Note:** The comparative clause (lines 7‑8) is realized in Malayalam as: **മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ്** *maraṇaṁ kuṟacc kūṭuthal āṇ* (“death is a little more”), preserving the ordering **death > bitter** and the slight degree **little**. The literal back‑translation check for each token is provided in the third column.

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Output: bullet list only; one line per source line. Format: - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Rules: each phrase is directly placeable (no glue-only fragments) and covers the line’s main predicate + required linkage. Hook: satisfy Step 2 requirements for that line (incl. back-translation checks). Comparatives: preserve ordering (A>B ⇔ B<A is OK) and degree; at least one phrase must make both recoverable. No punctuation inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ കയ്പ്പുള്ള ആണ് / കയ്പ്പുള്ളത് മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ് / മരണം കയ്പ്പുള്ളതിനെക്കാൾ കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ് - Line 8: പക്ഷേ ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയ നല്ലത് ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ വേണ്ടി / പക്ഷേ നല്ലത് അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ വേണ്ടി / പക്ഷേ ഞാൻ അവിടെ നല്ലത് കണ്ടെത്തി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ - Line 9: ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റ് വസ്തുക്കൾ പറയാം / ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റുള്ളവയെക്കുറിച്ച് പറയും / ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റ് കാര്യങ്ങൾ പറയും

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Task: Assemble Step3 phrases into Malayalam lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 phrases as contiguous substrings; reorder within line as needed. Allowed edits: insert only function-words/morphology for grammatical joining; no new content words. Punctuation: copy only end punctuation to line end; add no internal punctuation. Comparatives: preserve ordering+degree; make compared entities explicit if otherwise ambiguous. Output per source line (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary Step3 phrase: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - മരണം കയ്പ്പുള്ളതിനെക്കാൾ കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ്
**Assembly Notes:** - Inserted the intensifier “ഇത്ര” before the phrase to render the “so” of the original.
**Target Text:** ഇത്ര മരണം കയ്പ്പുള്ളതിനെക്കാൾ കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ്
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - പക്ഷേ നല്ലത് അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ വേണ്ടി
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional words needed; the phrase already contains the coordinating conjunction “പക്ഷേ” and the purpose marker “വേണ്ടി”.
**Target Text:** പക്ഷേ നല്ലത് അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ വേണ്ടി
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റ് വസ്തുക്കൾ പറയാം
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra function‑words required; the phrase supplies the subject, locative, object and future verb.
**Target Text:** ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റ് വസ്തുക്കൾ പറയാം

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check For each line: verify Step4 Target Text vs Reference Translation + Step1 Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within line; add only function-words/morphology; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation: keep only end punctuation from source; no internal punctuation. Output per line bullets with EXACT fields (no extras): Line #, Target Text, Back-Translation, Reference Translation, Checks, Corrected Target Text (if any). Checks: End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text MUST make all checks OK if possible. Comparative Orientation: preserve ordering+degree; treat (A>B) ≡ (B<A) and (A<B) ≡ (B>A); FAIL only if ordering reversed or degree lost. After all lines: if any line still FAILs, output UNVERIFIED with failing Line #s; otherwise do not output UNVERIFIED. Output final Malayalam text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line #: 7 Target Text: ഇത്ര മരണം കയ്പ്പുള്ളതിനെക്കാൾ കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ് Back-Translation: “So death is a little more than bitter.” Reference Translation: So bitter is it that death is little more. Checks: End Punct FAIL | Coverage OK | Meaning Drift OK | Comparative Orientation OK | Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text: ഇത്ര മരണം കയ്പ്പുള്ളതിനെക്കാൾ കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ്;
- Line #: 8 Target Text: പക്ഷേ നല്ലത് അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ വേണ്ടി Back-Translation: “But good there found to discuss for.” Reference Translation: But in order to treat of the good that there I found, Checks: End Punct FAIL | Coverage OK | Meaning Drift OK | Comparative Orientation N/A | Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text: പക്ഷേ നല്ലത് അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ വേണ്ടി,
- Line #: 9 Target Text: ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റ് വസ്തുക്കൾ പറയാം Back-Translation: “I will tell the other things I saw there.” Reference Translation: I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. Checks: End Punct FAIL | Coverage OK | Meaning Drift OK | Comparative Orientation N/A | Hallucination OK Corrected Target Text: ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റ് വസ്തുക്കൾ പറയാം.
``` ഇത്ര മരണം കയ്പ്പുള്ളതിനെക്കാൾ കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ ആണ്; പക്ഷേ നല്ലത് അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ വേണ്ടി, ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റ് വസ്തുക്കൾ പറയാം. ```
